people.name: Maya Chen
people.bio: Oil painter and reluctant early riser. I host the creekside sessions at Fish Creek and will absolutely talk your ear off about colour temperature.

people.name: Jamie Lee
people.bio: Quiet sessions, small sketchbooks, no small talk until the coffee break.

people.name: Sam Wilson
people.bio: Urban sketcher. Skylines, bridges, anything with a hard edge against a soft sky. Golden hour or nothing.

people.name: Priya Shah
people.bio: Botanical ink and the occasional very bad landscape. Mostly here for the walks.

people.name: Alex Laurent
people.bio: Watercolours, mostly. Happiest on a riverbank before the light gets flat. Trying to paint outside once a week, rain or snow.

spots.name: Fish Creek Provincial Park
spots.about: Follow the creek to quiet bends, open meadows and cottonwood groves. There’s room to set up an easel and plenty of changing light to keep you inspired.

spots.name: North Glenmore Park
spots.about: Wide water, long sightlines and the Rockies on a clear afternoon. The light turns over quickly here, which makes it a good place to practise working fast.

spots.name: Crescent Heights Lookout
spots.about: The classic downtown view across the Bow. Come for the last hour of light, when the towers warm up and the river goes silver.

spots.name: Bowness Park
spots.about: A gentle lagoon ringed by old poplars. Sheltered enough for windy days, and the reflections hold still long enough to draw.

spots.name: Nose Hill Park
spots.about: Grassland above the city with nothing to block the horizon. Bring something to weigh your paper down — it is always windier than it looks.

spots.name: Inglewood Bird Sanctuary
spots.about: Dense river forest with dappled light and somewhere new to look every few steps. The quietest spot on this list by a long way.

spots.name: Lake Louise Shoreline
spots.about: The most painted view in Alberta, and still worth it. Arrive before nine if you want the water flat and the shoreline to yourself.

spots.name: Vermilion Lakes
spots.about: Three shallow lakes with Rundle standing over them. Pull-outs along the road mean you can paint from beside the car on a cold day.

spots.name: Maligne Lake
spots.about: A long day from Calgary and worth every hour. The light moves fast between the peaks, so work small and work quickly.

spots.name: Horseshoe Canyon
spots.about: Stripes of ochre, grey and rust cut a hundred metres into flat prairie. A gift if you have been meaning to practise warm neutrals.

spots.name: Writing-on-Stone
spots.about: Hoodoos above the Milk River, and some of the oldest rock art on the continent. A quiet, serious place — paint the landforms, not the petroglyphs.

spots.name: Waterton Lakes Townsite
spots.about: Nowhere else in Alberta do mountains rise straight out of grassland with no foothills in between. Composition does half the work for you.

spots.name: North Saskatchewan River Valley
spots.about: The longest stretch of urban parkland in Canada. Bridges, river and skyline all in one view, with somewhere to stand for every one of them.

spots.name: Abraham Lake
spots.about: An unreal blue, and in deep winter the methane bubbles stack under the ice. Exposed and cold — this is a hardy-painters-only spot.

spots.name: Cypress Hills
spots.about: Lodgepole pine six hundred metres above the surrounding plain — an island of forest in the middle of grassland.

spots.name: Moraine Lake
spots.about: The view from the rockpile is the one on the old twenty-dollar bill. Shuttle only now, which has made it far calmer than it used to be.

spots.name: Peyto Lake Overlook
features: Cold and windy at the rail
spots.about: A wolf-head of meltwater seen from four hundred metres above it. The colour is genuinely hard to mix — bring more cerulean than you think.

spots.name: Two Jack Lake
spots.about: Quieter than its famous neighbours and a far better place to actually work. The lakeshore pull-outs let you paint from beside the car.

spots.name: Athabasca Falls
spots.about: Not tall, but enormously powerful, and the quartzite gorge below it is the real subject. Spray reaches further than you expect — mind your paper.

spots.name: Pyramid Lake
spots.about: A small wooden bridge to a pine island, with Pyramid Mountain behind it. One of the few spots up here that is easy to compose.

spots.name: Upper Kananaskis Lake
spots.about: Everything Banff has without the coaches. Drowned stumps along the shoreline give you foreground for free, which is rarer than it sounds.

spots.name: Policeman’s Creek, Canmore
spots.about: A slow creek running through town with the Three Sisters standing over it, and a coffee thirty seconds away. The easiest mountain painting in Alberta.

spots.name: Frank Slide
spots.about: Eighty million tonnes of limestone across a valley floor, and a town underneath it. A sober place, and an extraordinary study in grey.

spots.name: Dinosaur Provincial Park
spots.about: Hoodoos and eroded coulees over the Red Deer River. Shadows move fast across the formations, so pick your moment and commit to it.

spots.name: Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump
spots.about: A long sandstone escarpment above open grassland, used for nearly six thousand years. Paint the land; be thoughtful about what it is.

spots.name: Sylvan Lake
spots.about: A proper lake town with a pier, a beach and an unbroken western horizon. Busy in July, entirely yours in October.

spots.name: Dry Island Buffalo Jump
spots.about: You drive across wheat fields and then the ground simply falls away. Almost nobody comes here, which is most of its appeal.

spots.name: Elk Island National Park
spots.about: Rolling aspen and kettle lakes forty minutes from Edmonton, with free-roaming bison. Keep a sensible distance and paint from the car if the herd is close.

spots.name: Lesser Slave Lake
spots.about: Big enough that the far shore disappears, and the sand goes on for kilometres. A good place to work on nothing but sky and water.

spots.name: Peace River Lookout
spots.about: A deep green valley cut through farmland, seen from the hill above town. The furthest spot on this list and the one most worth the drive.

spots.name: Lac La Biche
spots.about: A causeway runs out to a wooded island in the middle of the lake. Pelicans in summer, and some of the quietest painting in the province.

events.title: Creekside Colour Study
events.headline: A morning of colour, creekside.
description: Let’s slow down and follow the light along Fish Creek. We’ll start with a few small colour studies, then find our own view to paint. Bring your favourite medium, a warm drink and a little curiosity.
We’ll meet at the Evergreen Hill trail entrance at 10:00 AM and walk down to the creek together. No instruction, no pressure — just a friendly group making art outside.

kit.title: Bring your outdoor kit
kit.body: Paints or sketchbook, a portable seat, layers and water.

weatherNote.title: Dress for a Calgary morning
weatherNote.body: We paint in cool weather. Check the chat for any last-minute changes.

events.pinned: Meet at the Evergreen Hill trail entrance. Bring warm layers!

events.title: Reservoir Light & Layers
events.headline: Chasing the last of the afternoon.
description: The reservoir gives you about ninety good minutes before the light drops behind the ridge. We’ll use them. Expect quick studies rather than finished pieces.
I’ll bring spare boards and a thermos. Come for all of it or just an hour.

kit.title: Pack light, work fast
kit.body: Small boards, a limited palette and something warm to sit on.

weatherNote.title: It is windier by the water
weatherNote.body: Clips or tape for your paper are worth the space in your bag.

events.pinned: Parking fills up fast — aim to arrive by 1:45 PM.

events.title: Skyline Sketch Social
events.headline: Draw the city, then go get a coffee.
description: A relaxed two hours at the lookout while the towers catch the last of the sun. Sketchbooks, pens, whatever you have.
We usually walk down to a café on Edmonton Trail afterwards. Entirely optional, always good.

kit.title: A sketchbook is plenty
kit.body: Pen or pencil, a folding stool if you have one, and gloves.

weatherNote.title: The lookout is exposed
weatherNote.body: It gets cold the moment the sun drops. Dress for after, not for now.

events.pinned: Sunset is 4:42 PM. Try to be set up by 4:00.

events.title: Quiet Morning, Quick Sketches
events.headline: Two hours, barely any talking.
description: For anyone who likes company but not conversation. We spread out along the creek, work for two hours, then compare pages at the end if you want to.
Arrive any time in the first twenty minutes.

kit.title: Whatever you can carry
kit.body: Sketchbook, one pen, and a flask of something hot.

weatherNote.title: Frost is likely
weatherNote.body: The creek path can be slippery first thing. Boots over trainers.

events.title: Woodland Ink Walk
events.headline: Stop every ten minutes. Draw what’s in front of you.
description: A slow loop of the sanctuary with five short stops. Five drawings, ten minutes each, no erasing.
It is a brilliant way to loosen up if your work has gone stiff.

kit.title: Ink, nib or brush pen
kit.body: Plus a small hardback sketchbook you can hold standing up.

weatherNote.title: Shade all the way round
weatherNote.body: It runs several degrees colder than the open park. Layer up.

events.title: Prairie Wide Horizons
events.headline: Nothing but horizon to get wrong.
description: A session about simplification: three bands, two values, one idea. Nose Hill is the right place to practise it.
We’ll regroup at the cairn at the end to look at everyone’s panels.

kit.title: Something to hold it all down
kit.body: Clips, tape, a weighted bag — the wind is the real subject here.

weatherNote.title: Fully exposed
weatherNote.body: There is no shelter on the hill. Windproof layers, properly.

events.title: Moraine Lake, First Light
events.headline: Up before the shuttle, out before the crowd.
description: The twenty minutes either side of sunrise are the whole reason to come. We will be set up on the rockpile before it starts.
Dress as though it is January, because at that hour it is.

kit.title: Cold-weather kit
kit.body: Gloves you can paint in, a headlamp and a flask.

weatherNote.title: Below freezing at dawn
weatherNote.body: Water-based media will slush. Oils or pencil are safer.

events.title: Kananaskis Snow Study
events.headline: Snow is not white. Come and prove it.
description: A session about seeing colour in snow — the blues in shadow, the warmth where the sun catches it. We will work small and compare at the end.
A conservation pass is required for the parking lot.

kit.title: Limited palette
kit.body: Two blues, one earth, white. That is genuinely enough.

weatherNote.title: Full winter conditions
weatherNote.body: Boots and traction. The lot is not always ploughed early.

events.title: Canmore Creek Hour
events.headline: One hour on the boardwalk, one hour in the café.
description: The lowest-commitment session we run. Draw the creek and the Three Sisters for an hour, then warm up over coffee with everyone.
Perfect if you have never done this before.

kit.title: A sketchbook and a pen
kit.body: That is the entire list. Borrow from us if you forget.

weatherNote.title: Sheltered, but cold
weatherNote.body: The boardwalk is out of the wind. Still bring a hat.

reviews.author: maya
reviews.body: The creek reflections are beautiful in the morning. Bring a warm layer and a small folding stool!

reviews.author: jamie
reviews.body: A favourite for colour studies. Lots of space, even with a group. The path is easy with an easel.

reviews.author: sam
reviews.body: Went down at sunrise and had the whole bend to myself. The cottonwoods are worth the walk.

reviews.author: priya
reviews.body: Huge skies. Get there an hour before sunset and you will not want to leave.

reviews.author: maya
reviews.body: Lovely light, but the wind off the water is no joke. Bring clips for your paper.

reviews.author: jamie
reviews.body: The best downtown view in the city and it is free. Busy at golden hour, worth it anyway.

messages.author: maya
messages.body: Hi everyone! So happy you’re joining on Saturday. We’ll meet at the Evergreen Hill entrance and walk to the creek together.

messages.author: jamie
messages.body: Looking forward to it! Is watercolour okay, or is this mostly an oil painting group?

messages.author: alex
messages.body: I’m bringing watercolours too, Jamie! Excited to finally paint this spot with a group.

messages.author: maya
messages.body: Every medium is welcome! A sketchbook is perfect too. See you by the trail! 🌿

messages.author: alex
messages.body: Boards and a thermos are sorted. Shout if you need anything else brought along.

messages.author: sam
messages.body: Added a café stop afterwards for anyone who fancies it.

gallery.title: Fish Creek, first frost
gallery.caption: Forty minutes before my hands gave out. The bank was all violets and I only noticed when I got home.

gallery.title: The Thursday crowd
gallery.caption: Eleven of us along the creek. Nobody said much for an hour, which was the point.

gallery.title: Glenmore, last light
gallery.caption: Tried to get the whole thing down in one sitting. Lost the sky, kept the water.

gallery.title: Downtown from Crescent Heights
gallery.caption: The towers go properly orange for about four minutes. This is minute three.

gallery.title: Palette after a long one
gallery.caption: Six hours of mixing greys. Worth photographing before I cleaned it off.

gallery.title: Study from the Icefields Parkway
gallery.caption: Painted from the back of the car with the heater on. Not ashamed of it.

gallery.title: Cottonwoods, late October
gallery.caption: Three sessions on the same bend. The third one finally held together.

gallery.title: Teaching the creekside group
gallery.caption: Eighteen people and one very patient thermos.

gallery.title: Moraine, before the shuttle
gallery.caption: Up at four. Painted in gloves. Would do it again tomorrow.

gallery.title: Horseshoe Canyon, raw sienna
gallery.caption: A whole painting out of four pigments. The badlands make that easy.

gallery.title: Scouting Bowness
gallery.caption: Walked the whole lagoon looking for a composition. Found three.

gallery.title: Bow Tower at 4:40pm
gallery.caption: Twelve minutes, standing up, one pen. The deadline is the point.

gallery.title: Sketch social, November
gallery.caption: Nine of us on the railing. Two had never drawn a building before.

gallery.title: Nose Hill, three bands
gallery.caption: Grass, hill, sky. I keep trying to make it simpler than that and failing.

gallery.title: Frank Slide
gallery.caption: Hard to draw somewhere that is also a grave. Took my time with this one.

gallery.title: Quiet morning, bridge four
gallery.caption: Two hours, nobody spoke, perfect.

gallery.title: Inglewood, dappled
gallery.caption: Light through poplars is almost impossible and I will keep trying.

gallery.title: Travel kit, finally sorted
gallery.caption: Twelve pans, one brush, fits in a coat pocket.

gallery.title: Elk Island, aspen study
gallery.caption: Stood very still for a long time. The bison moved on eventually.

gallery.title: River valley, early
gallery.caption: Edmonton does mornings better than anyone gives it credit for.

gallery.title: Woodland ink walk, test run
gallery.caption: Five stops, ten minutes each, no erasing. Harder than it sounds.
